questionText: What is the difference between REST and SOAP?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can compare REST as an architectural style with SOAP as an XML messaging framework without reducing the choice to JSON versus XML or claiming automatic enterprise capabilities.
outOfScope: A claim that REST requires JSON
A claim that SOAP itself guarantees security, reliability, or transactions
A claim that every SOAP body is RPC-shaped

claims.statement: REST is an architectural style defined through constraints including client-server separation, statelessness, cacheability, a uniform interface, layers, and optional code on demand.
SOAP 1.2 is a messaging framework whose XML Envelope contains an optional Header followed by a required Body and whose specification defines processing and fault rules.
REST transfers representations using dynamically selected data types and does not require JSON; using XML does not by itself make an interaction SOAP or prevent REST constraints.
Apart from SOAP Fault, SOAP 1.2 Part 1 does not mandate one structure or interpretation for Body child elements, so application payloads are not inherently limited to RPC operations.

A SOAP envelope alone does not establish an application's authentication, authorization, reliable-delivery, or transaction guarantees; those require additional agreed specifications and implementation.

examples.title: Minimal SOAP 1.2 envelope with one application payload

validation.command: Parse the XML and verify the SOAP 1.2 namespace, one Envelope, and one Body
validation.expected: Well-formed SOAP 1.2 XML whose GetCustomer child is explicitly application-defined

visuals.title: Architectural style versus structured messaging framework

notes: The WSDL and WS-* discussion is intentionally described as commonly paired or separately agreed, not inherent SOAP behavior.

review.notes: REST claims were checked against Fielding; SOAP structure and payload boundaries were checked against SOAP 1.2 Part 1.
